# dash-gen

Registry-driven generator for the development dash. Reads the single source of truth — [`_data/projects.yml`](../../../_data/projects.yml) — and:

- **`health`** → gathers live GitHub signals (stars, CI build stats, issues, PRs, commit activity, security alerts, latest release) per project, computes an **attention level** (red/amber/green + reasons) from [`_data/health_thresholds.yml`](../../../_data/health_thresholds.yml), and writes `_data/project_health.yml`. This file is **ephemeral** — generated at deploy time, gitignored, never committed.
- **`readme`** → rewrites only the `<!-- AUTO:projects -->` span of the profile [`README.md`](../../../README.md) from the registry's static facts. Deterministic and safe to commit. `--check` fails (non-zero) if the span is stale instead of writing — used by the drift gate.
- **`ai`** → shadow-prices local Claude Code usage per repo ([`ai_activity.py`](ai_activity.py)). Scans the per-session JSONL ledgers under `~/.claude/projects/`, dedupes streamed records, attributes each turn to a repo via its `cwd` (worktrees/submodules normalized), max-merges daily aggregates into a **persistent ledger** (`~/.claude/ai-activity-ledger.json`, so history survives Claude Code's ~30-day transcript cleanup), and writes `_data/ai_activity.yml` — **ephemeral**, gitignored, rendered by the `/ai-activity/` dash page. Costs are estimates at Anthropic API list prices (subscription usage bills nothing per token). **Local-only**: not part of `all`, never runs in CI, and spend data is never committed or published.
- **`actions`** → GitHub Actions usage analytics ([`actions_analytics.py`](actions_analytics.py)). Queries the Actions API for every registry repo via the **PyGithub** integration library, aggregates per-workflow consumption (wall-clock minutes, success/failure, **effectiveness** = share of minutes ending in success, **waste** = minutes on non-success runs), groups by workflow **type**, flags "high-running, low-effective" workflows, and writes `_data/actions_usage.yml` — rendered by the `/actions/` dash page. Unlike `health`/`ai`, this file is **committed** and refreshed **daily** by [`fleet-pulse.yml`](../../workflows/fleet-pulse.yml) so the page shows a stable once-a-day snapshot. Auth via `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` or `gh auth token`. A workflow with **no verdicts** in the window (every run skipped by an `if:` gate) reports `success_rate_pct` / `effectiveness_pct` as **null**, not `0.0` — "no data" and "failed every run" must not render identically. Each record also carries `last_conclusion` (the verdict that stands today) and `dispatch_pct` (share of hand-triggered runs), which is what `remediate` filters false positives on. The wall-clock **cost proxy is bounded**, because unbounded elapsed time is wrong in exactly one direction — a run that never reaches a runner bills nothing but keeps accruing: a run that did not execute (`startup_failure`, or zero jobs) contributes **0 minutes**, and every other run is clamped to `MAX_RUN_MIN` (360, GitHub's own per-job ceiling). Only the MINUTES are zeroed — such runs still count toward `success_rate_pct` and the `failing` flag, since they genuinely are red. The job count costs one request, so it is asked **only** of runs whose wall clock already exceeds the cap, which keeps that spend proportional to the handful of outliers per sweep rather than to every run — the same objection that keeps the per-run `/timing` lookup out. Finally, the fleet `totals` range over **bamr87-owned workflows only**, the same population as the `by_type`/`by_repo`/`by_day` rollups. Both bounds are load-bearing: one run parked non-terminal for 68h at `billable: {}` once contributed 4079.9 phantom minutes and took over the fix queue, while summing waste over *all* workflows against an owned-only denominator published 2091.6h wasted against 1269.3h consumed and an impossible **-64.8%** effectiveness ([#229](https://github.com/bamr87/bamr87/issues/229)). Fixture tests: `python3 test_actions_analytics.py`.
- **`ai-usage`** → the COMMITTED fleet Claude Code ledger ([`ai_usage_collector.py`](ai_usage_collector.py)). Harvests every Claude touchpoint in public infrastructure: workflow runs of `anthropics/claude-code-action` in any registry repo (auto-detected from workflow content; **cost + turn counts scraped from run logs** — CI logs carry no token breakdown), commits with a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer, and PRs carrying the Claude Code marker. Writes `_data/ai_usage.yml` (committed, refreshed daily by [`fleet-pulse.yml`](../../workflows/fleet-pulse.yml)), rendered by `/ai-usage/`. Run it **locally** to also fold the machine ledger's aggregate into the `local` section (an explicit publish); the CI refresh preserves that section without adding to it.
- **`daily`** → prior-day fleet activity digest + failure work order ([`daily_report.py`](daily_report.py)). Scans every registry repo (PyGithub) for the window's commits, PRs, issues, releases, and CI failures; writes the **committed** digest `_reports/daily/<date>.md` (+ regenerates the `_reports/README.md` index span) and an ephemeral, **deduped** failure work order for the [`fleet-pulse.yml`](../../workflows/fleet-pulse.yml) agent.
- **`triage`** → fleet-wide OPEN-state snapshot ([`fleet_triage.py`](fleet_triage.py)). Inventories every registry repo's open issues (items + labels/age), open PRs (draft/dependabot/CI status), and each workflow's latest completed conclusion; computes a deterministic per-repo attention score and a prioritized cross-fleet **inbox**; writes `_data/fleet_triage.yml` — **committed**, refreshed daily by the same `fleet-pulse.yml` run, rendered by the `/triage/` portal page. External mirrors are excluded from totals/scores/inbox.
- **`estimate`** → client-engagement estimates ([`engagements.py`](engagements.py)). Treats every registry project as a client: sweeps open issues from the committed triage snapshot (offline; `--repo`/`--issue` narrow it, single issues fall back to `gh api`), classifies each deterministically (**estimator-v1**: labels/title → type → tier, per-repo calibration from `ai_usage.yml`), prices it from the rate card `_data/engagement_rates.yml` (AI tokens at API list prices + human **broker** hours + CI minutes + confidence contingency, with a pre-AI `traditional` comparison → **leverage**), and appends draft engagements (status: `estimated` — proposals a human approves) to `_data/engagements.yml` — **committed**, rendered at `/engagements/`. Idempotent: same snapshot in, byte-identical file out. See [`docs/ESTIMATION.md`](../../../docs/ESTIMATION.md).
- **`ledger`** → engagement actuals + variance ([`engagements.py`](engagements.py)). Accrues auditable evidence — `ai_usage.yml` CI runs (real cost), Claude commits/PRs, plus this machine's ai-activity ledger unless `--no-local` — into each approved/in-progress/delivered engagement (URL-deduped, oldest-open-first attribution), recomputes actual cost (AI + broker hours + platform), variance bands, and the per-client + fleet rollups. Also the status console: `--set-status ENG-NNNN=<status>` (validated lifecycle) and `--broker ENG-NNNN=<hours>`. Runs daily in CI via `fleet-pulse.yml` right after the evidence harvest.
- **`remediate`** → the fleet-doctor fix queue ([`remediation.py`](remediation.py)). Merges the two ACTIONABLE signals into ONE ranked list: **standing failures** from `_data/fleet_triage.yml` (every workflow whose latest run is red — so a workflow broken for weeks stays queued, which a prior-day-only scan misses) and **cost flags** from `_data/actions_usage.yml` (`slow`/`flaky`/`cancel-heavy`/`cron-heavy`/`high-cost-low-value`, plus an absolute long-running bar from `_data/fleet.yml`). Candidates are keyed on `owner/repo:workflow-path`, so a workflow that is both red **and** expensive is a single entry carrying both signals rather than two competing tickets — the failure mode of the two split loops this replaces. Each is classified `hub` (fixable in the checkout) or `submodule` (needs a cross-repo PR), ranked by severity then wasted minutes, deduped against open issues **and** open PRs in both the hub and the target repo (retired `actions-review`/`daily-analysis` markers honoured, so pre-migration tickets aren't re-filed), and capped by `remediation.max_candidates` / `max_cross_repo`. Externality is derived from the repo owner, never read from the data's `external` flag — that field is absent from older snapshots and a missing key is falsey, which would quietly admit upstream mirrors into a queue that opens PRs. Three guards filter the queue, all switched in `_data/fleet.yml` → `remediation:`: **`supersede_on_success`** drops `failing`/`flaky` when the workflow's latest non-skipped run was green (a 14-day average has no memory of order, so a bug fixed fifteen minutes later still scores 33% success); **`interactive_dispatch_pct`** drops the cost signals — and the `min_priority` fallback — when most runs were hand-dispatched, because a debugging session is expected to fail and to burn minutes; and **`stale_after_days`** de-prioritises a candidate whose latest run on record is older than the threshold, because a workflow triggered rarely (`issues: opened`, `workflow_dispatch`, a weekly cron) cannot clear its own red and would otherwise hold a slot forever. The third one only DOWN-RANKS — suppress on positive evidence of health, down-rank on absence of evidence — so a dispatch-only deploy that really has been broken for three weeks keeps its coverage, annotated with its age and sorted below every live candidate of the same severity. It reads both signals' timestamp formats (ISO-8601-with-offset from `actions_usage.yml`, `"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC"` from `fleet_triage.yml`) and treats an unreadable one as fresh. Absent the supporting fields (`last_conclusion`, `dispatch_pct`, `last_run_at`, added alongside), older snapshots behave exactly as before. See [`docs/DAILY-ANALYSIS.md`](../../../docs/DAILY-ANALYSIS.md#three-guards-on-the-queue). Emits `remediation-workorder.md` (ephemeral) for [`fleet-pulse.yml`](../../workflows/fleet-pulse.yml)'s `doctor` job. Fixture tests: `python3 test_remediation.py`. The queue's **consumer** is guarded separately by `python3 test_fleet_pulse_doctor.py` — the cap here is only useful if the `doctor` agent is funded to work through it, so that test asserts `remediation.max_candidates`, the workflow's shadowing `--limit` fallback, and `--max-turns` stay in step, and that every command the agent's prompt instructs is actually in its `--allowedTools`. Both invariants failed silently in production before it existed.
- **`harness`** → the six-layer harness health scorecard + trip wires ([`harness.py`](harness.py)). The self-observation half of Layer 6 ([`docs/HARNESS.md`](../../../docs/HARNESS.md)): **offline and deterministic** — reads only the committed fleet signals (`actions_usage.yml`, `fleet_triage.yml`, `issue_pipeline.yml`, `token_rotation.yml`), computes the playbook's health scorecard (completion rate, effectiveness, waste, cost per verified run, standing failures, escalations, credential age) and evaluates the trip wires declared in `_data/fleet.yml` `harness:` (`stale-data`, `pass-rate-floor`, `waste-ceiling`, `cost-spike` — fleet-**median**-relative with an absolute floor — `standing-failures`, `credential-overdue`). Writes the **committed** `_data/harness_health.yml`, refreshed daily as the LAST gather step of [`fleet-pulse.yml`](../../workflows/fleet-pulse.yml)'s `pulse` job so a degraded signal above it trips `stale-data` instead of failing the step. A tripped wire is an attention item, never an action — the doctor/pipeline/rotation loops own the fixes. Fixture tests: `python3 test_harness.py`.
- **`harnesses`** → the fleet AI-harness + schedule inventory ([`harness_registry.py`](harness_registry.py)). The output is a **consumed interface** — GitFactory's Fleet Studio (bamr87/gitorio specs/012) reads it as its fleet roster — so it opens with `schema: harness-registry/v1` (additive changes free; renames/removals bump it) and records GitFactory provenance per repo (`factory`, `factory_blueprints` from `.factory/`) and per harness (`factory: {blueprint, hash}` from the `⚙ GENERATED BY GITFACTORY` header, `switch` = the `vars.*_ENABLED` kill switch; a scheduled agent without one is a `switch-missing` finding). The DEPLOYMENT-side counterpart of `harness` (which watches the hub's own layers): scans every registry repo's `.github/workflows/` (PyGithub) for `claude-code-action` call sites — kind (mention-handler / scheduled-agent / event-agent, where "mention" requires a mention-capable trigger, not just the string `@claude` in a comment), action ref, **OAuth-first auth shape**, model/turn budget, and the `# kit: agent-context vX.Y.Z` stamp graded against `templates/agent-context/VERSION` — plus **every cron in the fleet**, normalized to estimated fires/day (documented approximation: weekly ≈ 1/7, dom ≈ k/30.44, both-restricted = capped OR). Joins the committed ledgers (`ai_usage.yml` cost, `actions_usage.yml` conclusions/flags, `token_rotation.yml` secret presence), then grades everything against `_data/fleet.yml` `harnesses:`: **baseline coverage** (mention handler / agent context / OAuth secret; external, archived, and `exempt:` repos are excused, not failed), **throughput** (estimated scheduled AI runs/day vs fleet + per-repo caps, UTC-hour adjacency), and **budget** (week-over-week trend + projected monthly vs ceilings). Writes the **committed** `_data/harness_registry.yml` (rendered at `/harnesses/`), refreshed daily by [`fleet-pulse.yml`](../../workflows/fleet-pulse.yml); without a token (or with `--offline`) it REUSES the previous committed scan and refreshes only the offline analytics. `--gaps` prints the fan-out-DEPLOYABLE gap repos one per line (missing handler/context, or an upgradeable machine seed — a missing secret is deliberately token-rotation's lane) — the plan input of [`harness-fanout.yml`](../../workflows/harness-fanout.yml) and `dash harnesses deploy --gaps`. Everything it emits is read-only observation with the lever named. Fixture tests: `python3 test_harness_registry.py`. See [`docs/HARNESS-OPS.md`](../../../docs/HARNESS-OPS.md).
- **`issues`** → the three-tier issue pipeline's queues ([`issue_pipeline.py`](issue_pipeline.py)). Sweeps every registry repo's open issues and pipeline PRs, derives each issue's **stage from its labels** (`agent:ready` / `agent:in-pr` / `agent:blocked` / `agent:hold` / `agent:done`), and computes — deterministically, before any model runs — the **gaps** blocking autonomous implementation (each tagged `agent`-closable or `human`-closable, which is exactly what separates `agent:ready` from `agent:blocked`), a readiness score, a type, a priority, a size, an owner, and an autonomy verdict (`auto` / `assisted` / `blocked`). Type detection reads the **title before the body**: matching over the concatenation let a 6 KB body's incidental `secrets.FLEET_TOKEN` retype a translation bug as security, forcing P0 and human review on a routine CI fix. An issue with an open pipeline PR is at tier 3 regardless of a stale `agent:ready` label, and a green non-draft PR leaves the tier-3 queue so the loop converges. Caps (`intake.max_issues` / `max_per_repo`, `implement.max_issues` / `max_cross_repo`, `complete.max_prs`) come from `_data/fleet.yml`. Writes the **committed** `_data/issue_pipeline.yml` (rendered at `/issue-pipeline/`) plus `issue-workorder-t{1,2,3}.md` (ephemeral) for [`issue-pipeline.yml`](../../workflows/issue-pipeline.yml)'s three agent tiers. `--sync-labels --apply` creates the taxonomy in every target repo — `gh issue edit --add-label` fails the *whole* call on one unknown label, so a missing label costs an issue its entire triage. Fixture tests: `python3 test_issue_pipeline.py`. See [`docs/ISSUE-PIPELINE.md`](../../../docs/ISSUE-PIPELINE.md).
- **`targets`** → the weekly repo-evolution plan ([`evolution.py`](evolution.py)). The deterministic half of [`repo-evolution.yml`](../../workflows/repo-evolution.yml), the same split `remediate`/`issues` use: selects registry entries that opted in (`auto_evolve: true`) **and** are owned, non-archived submodules — an external mirror is refused whatever the registry says, the guard `tools/fanout.sh` applies — skips any repo whose previous evolution PR is still open (branch prefix `ai-evolution/` or the hidden `<!-- repo-evolution key="owner/repo" -->` marker; one draft per repo is the backpressure, `--no-dedupe` for offline/`force`), caps per `_data/fleet.yml` `evolution.max_targets` (drops are reported, never silent), and writes each survivor a **brief** — `evolution-workorders/evolution-workorder-<name>.md` (ephemeral): the marker first, registry facts, the fleet's current signals for the repo from `_data/fleet_triage.yml` (attention, failing workflows, open issues bugs-first, open PRs minus dependabot — quoted as context and fenced off as the doctor's / issue pipeline's lanes), the operator's `--focus`, then the rendered goals template and category emphasis from [`.github/evolution/`](../../evolution/). Stdout is one JSON plan (`include` matrix + `max_parallel`/`max_turns`/`branch_prefix`/`label`/`marker` from `fleet.yml`, so each knob is stated once); everything human-readable goes to stderr. An explicit `--target` that yields nothing exits 1. Fixture + workflow-contract tests: `python3 test_evolution.py` (asserts the workflow's cron, wiring, allowlist, draft-only publish, and lockfile guard against `fleet.yml`). See [`docs/EVOLUTION.md`](../../../docs/EVOLUTION.md).
- **`vendor`** → the vendored Pyramid Schema kit vs upstream ([`schema_vendor.py`](schema_vendor.py)). The hub does not depend on [bamr87/SCHEMA](https://github.com/bamr87/SCHEMA), it **copies** from it — the linter into `tools/schema_lint.py`, the seed template and protocol snippet into `templates/schema/` — and `templates/schema/VERSION` recorded the provenance **by hand**. `tools/check-drift.sh` check (i) compares each submodule's copy against the HUB's; nothing compared the hub's against UPSTREAM, so the whole fleet could sit a year behind the package it vendors with every gate green. This reads upstream's content-addressed `DISTRIBUTION.yml` and grades each file at the parity the manifest declares: **strict** (`schema_lint.py`) must be byte-identical and is re-vendored by `--apply`; **text** (template, snippet) may be reflowed/requoted here — deliberately — but not changed in substance, and drift there is reported for a human, never auto-written, because an overwrite would throw the local adaptation away every week. A restamp of `VERSION` is surgical: three provenance lines, comments and notes intact. Upstream unreachable exits **2**, distinct from drift's **1**, so a network blip cannot open a PR. Driven weekly by [`schema-vendor.yml`](../../workflows/schema-vendor.yml). Fixture tests (no network — upstream is a dict and a lambda): `python3 test_schema_vendor.py`.
- **`reconcile`** → registry ↔ GitHub reconciliation ([`reconcile.py`](reconcile.py)). Compares three sources — the registry's `repo_url`, the `.gitmodules` url, and GitHub itself — then routes each finding by how trustworthy the signal is. **Authoritative** drift (a repo *renamed* on GitHub; a registry↔`.gitmodules` *url mismatch*) is written by `--apply` through surgical line edits that preserve the registry's comments and formatting. **Advisory** drift (*404s*, *branch drift*) is reported and never auto-applied: a repo-scoped token 404s on a private repo exactly as it does on a deleted one, and this fleet intentionally tracks non-default branches (`scripts`=`master`, `sonic-pi`=`dev`). Driven nightly by [`reconcile-registry.yml`](../../workflows/reconcile-registry.yml), which opens a PR for the authoritative fixes and a tracking issue for the rest. `--json` emits the machine-readable contract that workflow consumes.
- **`cv`** → the fleet's CV portfolio fragment ([`cv_fragment.py`](cv_fragment.py)). Projects the registry into [bamr87/cv](https://github.com/bamr87/cv)'s data contract: **committed** `_data/cv_portfolio.json` holds CVData-shaped `Project[]` (featured always, else `status: active`; archived never) plus a rollup `Skill` group of every non-archived stack. It is a deterministic **proposal**, not a direct write — the `sync-cv` skill (or a human) reviews it against that repo's `data/cv.json`, fills `startDate`, strips the adoption-metadata keys (`featured`, `fleet_status`), and merges what belongs on the CV. Fixture tests: `python3 -m pytest test_cv_fragment.py`.
- **`lake`** → the LOCAL data lake + the Phoenix trace exporter ([`fleet_lake.py`](fleet_lake.py)), the local stack's "download what GitHub holds" half ([`docs/HARNESS-OPS.md`](../../../docs/HARNESS-OPS.md), "The local stack"). `lake sync` (PyGithub) upserts, per owned registry repo + the hub, into `.dash-lake/fleet.sqlite` (`DASH_LAKE_DIR`; **gitignored, never committed** — it holds logs): the repo row (`.factory/` and `fleet.manifest.yml` presence), every workflow file classified with `harness_registry` (kind, auth, `vars.*_ENABLED` kill switch, GitFactory `blueprint@hash` provenance; unchanged blobs are reclassified from the stored text without a second fetch), the `.factory/**` design tree, workflow runs → jobs → steps (refreshed until a run completes, then final), the run-log zip entry by entry under a per-run byte cap, the **claude-code-action facts** parsed from those logs even with the action's default `show_full_output: false` (SDK options → `maxTurns` + tool grants, the `init` block → resolved model, the `result` block → turns/cost/duration/denials, the session id; with full output also assistant turns and tool calls with their log-line timestamps), and the window's issues/PRs. `--jobs`/`--logs ai|all|none` size the API spend (default: AI runs only). `lake status [--json]` is the console's `/api/lake` document — tables, freshness, per-repo counts, agent spend/models, the export ledger, Phoenix reachability. `lake export` builds **OpenInference** spans — per CI run: run → job → step, the Claude step as the `AGENT` span with model/tokens/cost/turns/grants, tool calls as `TOOL` spans when present; with `--local`, per `~/.claude/projects` transcript: session → every assistant turn (`LLM`, tokens + shadow cost) → every tool call closed by its `tool_result` — and ships them over OTLP/HTTP to Phoenix (`PHOENIX_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT`, default `http://127.0.0.1:6006`; `PHOENIX_API_KEY` forwarded, never printed). Trace/span ids are **deterministic** (sha256 of the run/session key), the `exports` ledger skips what was shipped unless `--force`, and `--dry-run` writes `.dash-lake/export-preview.json` with no OpenTelemetry dependency. Fixture tests: `python3 test_fleet_lake.py` (log parsing, ids, span trees, transcript parsing, idempotent upserts, ledger gating, console documents).
- **`all`** → `health` then `readme`.

## Usage

```bash
pip install -r .github/scripts/dash-gen/requirements.txt
gh auth login                       # health needs GitHub API access (or GH_TOKEN in CI)

python .github/scripts/dash-gen/dash_gen.py health
python .github/scripts/dash-gen/dash_gen.py readme [--check]
python .github/scripts/dash-gen/dash_gen.py ai [--window 30] [--ledger PATH] [--claude-dir PATH]

# or via the wrapper:
tools/dash-gen health
tools/dash-gen readme
tools/dash-gen ai        # also: tools/dash ai
tools/dash-gen ai-usage --days 14  # committed fleet Claude ledger (/ai-usage/)
tools/dash-gen actions --days 14   # also: tools/dash actions
tools/dash-gen daily --days 1      # also: tools/dash daily (digest + work order)
tools/dash-gen triage              # also: tools/dash triage (open-state snapshot, /triage/)
tools/dash-gen harness             # also: tools/dash harness (scorecard + trip wires, offline)
tools/dash-gen harnesses           # also: tools/dash harnesses (fleet harness+schedule inventory, /harnesses/)
tools/dash-gen harnesses --gaps    # fan-out-deployable gap repos (feeds harness-fanout / dash harnesses deploy)
tools/dash-gen lake sync --days 7  # also: tools/dash lake sync (GitHub → .dash-lake/fleet.sqlite, local only)
tools/dash-gen lake status         # what the lake holds + Phoenix reachability (--json for the console)
tools/dash-gen lake export --local --dry-run   # OpenInference traces → Phoenix (:6006); dry run previews
tools/dash-gen estimate --limit 10 # also: tools/dash estimate (draft engagement estimates)
tools/dash-gen ledger              # also: tools/dash ledger (accrue actuals + variance)
tools/dash-gen cv [--check]        # registry -> _data/cv_portfolio.json (bamr87/cv sync proposal)
tools/dash-gen targets --no-dedupe # also: tools/dash gen targets (repo-evolution plan + briefs, offline)
```

GitHub access uses the `gh` CLI, so failures degrade gracefully (a project that can't be reached yields nulls, not a crash).
